expectation: Membrane rings on nearly all nucleated cells (epithelium, stroma, immune, endothelium), so it is ubiquitous rather than a subset. Crypt/villus epithelium should show crisp honeycomb outlines, and some tumour cells may be dim or negative. Nuclei should be unstained.
observed: A: both sections are lit, with crypt architecture visible, plus glow on the glass. B and C: sharp membrane honeycomb on the epithelium, with unstained nuclei and a dark lumen. D: blurred haze. E: membrane rings beside and over some CD31 vessels; stroma is hazy.
why: B and C show crisp membrane rings outlining epithelial cells with unstained nuclei, which is the expected ubiquitous membrane pattern for HLA-A, not haze or grain.
notes: Strong, sharp membrane honeycomb on crypt epithelium, with clear nuclei, as expected for HLA class I. Off-tissue glass glow and a blurry D field are artefacts that do not undermine the cellular pattern.
